captions.instagram:
How does an inverter or UPS work?

When the power cuts out and the fans keep turning, a box in the corner is quietly turning a battery's DC back into 230 V AC. Take a home inverter and a computer UPS apart in 3D, and watch the switch happen in milliseconds.

→ A home inverter stores electricity in a battery while the mains is on.
→ When the power cuts out, the battery’s DC is turned back into AC for your fans and lights.
→ Four diodes flip the backwards half of every AC wave, and a capacitor smooths the bumps into DC.
→ Four switches flip the battery back and forth fifty times a second: that makes AC.
→ Pure sine inverters switch thousands of times a second, then smooth the pulses into a clean wave.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/upsclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does an inverter or UPS work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
When the power cuts out and the fans keep turning, a box in the corner is quietly turning a battery's DC back into 230 V AC. Take a home inverter and a computer UPS apart in 3D, and watch the switch happen in milliseconds.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/upsclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/upsclear

In this video:
• Store it now, give it back later. A home inverter is a battery, a charger and an inverter in one box.
• AC into DC: four diodes and a capacitor. Mains in India swings between +325 V and −325 V fifty times a second.
• DC into AC: four switches and a transformer. Four MOSFET switches in an H-bridge connect the battery one way round, then the other, 50 times a second.
• Switching over in milliseconds. An offline UPS lets mains straight through and clicks a relay over to its inverter when the mains fails, in about 5 to 15 ms.
• How long the backup lasts. 12 V × 150 Ah is 1,800 Wh, but only about 80% is usable, the inverter loses about 15%, and draining a battery fast gives less capacity (Peukert's law).
• Inside the battery. Six lead-acid cells of about 2.1 V make 12.6 V.
